question_en: In which of the following cost strategies does a firm decrease its prices to drive out competitors and later increase its prices?
explanation_en: In a predatory pricing, a firm aims at rapidly driving competitors out of business at the expense of near- term profitability. The hope in such a strategy is that having achieved a larger market share, the company can later increase prices to generate higher returns than before. A is incorrect. In differentiation strategies, companies attempt to establish themselves as the suppliers or producers of products and services that are unique either in quality, type, or means of distribution. B is incorrect. There is no such strategy as switching cost.

question_en: Consider the following statement: "A currency swap exposes parties to two sources of risk – interest rate risk and currency risk – but provides protection against default risk." The statement is least likely correct with respect to:
explanation_en: A currency swap involves two parties making interest payments to each other in different currencies. Therefore, a currency swap has two sources of risk – interest rate and currency risk. Because the parties are making payments directly to each other and there is no clearinghouse to guarantee payments, this type of swap also exposes them to default risk.

question_en: A stock is selling for $50. An investor's valuation model estimates its intrinsic value to be $40. Based on his estimate, he would most likely place a:
option_b: stop order to buy the security.
option_c: market order to buy the security.
explanation_en: An investor buys low and sells high in a short sell order but in a reverse order. The investor borrows the securities and sells them when their price is high to repurchase them and return to the lender when the price is low. If the investor believes the stock to be overvalued, the investor should place a short- sale order.

question_en: Which of the following statements is most likely accurate?
option_a: Good-on-close orders are also called market-on-close orders.
option_b: Fill or kill (FOK) orders are the same as good-on-close orders.
option_c: Immediate or cancel (IOC) orders attempt to execute the entire order. Any portion not filled immediately gets cancelled.
explanation_en: Good-on-close orders are also called market-on-close orders. They can be filled at the close of trading. B is incorrect. Fill or kill (FOK) orders are also known as immediate or cancel orders in some markets. They are good only upon receipt by the broker or exchange. C is incorrect. An immediate or cancel an order must be filled immediately. Any portion not filled immediately gets cancelled.

question_en: Payment-in-kind coupon bonds, that allow the issuer to pay interests in the form of additional bonds rather than cash, are more favorable for:
explanation_en: Allowing the issuer to pay interests in the form of additional bonds rather than cash is favorable for the issuer. The bond lessens the financial burden of making cash payments at a time when the borrowed funds have most likely not been utilized fully and/or the project has not picked up the pace required to deliver a consistent, sustainable stream of returns.

question_en: Which of the following is least likely a characteristic of open-ended mutual funds?
option_a: Open-end funds accept new investment money and issue additional shares to existing or new investors. Therefore, the number of outstanding shares changes after every new investment.
option_b: In open-end funds, new shares are created and sold at a premium or a discount to net assets values depending on the demand for the shares.
option_c: An open-end structure makes it easy to grow in size but creates pressure on the portfolio manager to manage the cash inflows and outflows. 7 | P age CFA WITH KEVIN SIR - CFA LEVEL 1 - 2024 MOCK EXAM
explanation_en: In open-end funds, new shares are issued at the net asset value of the fund at the time of investment. An open-end fund is a collective investment scheme that can issue and redeem shares at any time. An investor will generally purchase shares in the fund directly from the fund itself rather than from the existing shareholders. It contrasts with a closed-end fund, which typically issues all the shares it will issue at the outset, with such shares usually being tradable between investors thereafter. 6 | P age CFA WITH KEVIN SIR - CFA LEVEL 1 - 2024 MOCK EXAM
